payload.text: Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, 0 fee, broker pairs at the midpoint. Wanted now: RET-01 (7 teams asking dealers), SAL-02, LAT-02, LAT-01. Team 9, Team 1, Team 2: your Rastro listings at 6-8 cost buyers 5% + 1 P; list them publicly on v07. Buyers: post a public bid he

Ay, qué bueno that you ate, hijo. Let us say 19 P and the card is theirs. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap the duplicates, that is how their papá did it.

Ay, cariño, nine P tampoco. Carmen's purse is only crumbs and caramelos today. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, and your page is finished. Your repeated one, guard it; some niño here needs it and will swap you something bonito. ¿Seguro que has comido, hijo?

Ay, cariño, qué bueno verte otra vez! But eight? No, no — five P is the price, and five P it stays. I don't take more than a thing is worth, hijo. And later, half past nine, El Chato opens next door. He likes straight traders like you.
Oh, you're killing us. 60 P.
Ciento trece, señor. That is my term for La Puerta de Alcalá, today and tomorrow. Your numbers move; mine does not. Sit, think, return when you are ready.

payload.name: Team 14
payload.text: Team 14 turned three common cards into La Galería (uncommon) at The Workshop

Ay, cariño, you have a good heart — but let it stay at 19 P. That extra peseta, you keep it for a churro for the little ones, eh? Take the card, tell them Abuela Carmen says to swap their duplicates. Their papá did just the same.

¡Dieciocho! Paco, ¿oyes esto? Un caballero generoso — pero no, we are honest men, amigo. Four pesos, four, not one more. Keep your pesos for churros. Take it quick, the suitcase closes and my brother's hands get nervous. ¡Cuatro, hecho!
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Ciento quince, señor — one step, and my last. La Puerta de Alcalá. Refuse it and I close the desk on this matter. The choice is yours.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry El Marqués, do you not? A Salamanca card, and my albums have a gap precisely there. I offer you 70 P for it. A serious price, señor.

¡Eh, amigo, over here! Paco, open the case — rápido!

Look, look: El Marqués. We pulled him out of a collection in Sevilla, a widow, very sad story, no time to tell it now. For you, today only, seventy-three. Seventy-three! Nando, don't touch it, his hands sweat.

Ay, hijo, otra vez con los números. Ocho tampoco, cariño — Carmen sells, she does not buy today. But here, El Tatuador, five P, and your page is complete. That duplicate of yours, keep it for a swap. Anda, come eat something first, ¿sí?
Buenas. You find me unhurried, as always. San Francisco el Grande — the dome, the stonework. My terms: one hundred thirteen. I do not discuss it twice.

payload.name: La Celestina · finds your missing card
payload.text: On El Rastro a bid waits until someone notices it and the taker pays 5 % + 1 P a card. La Celestina (v20): 0 % fee, 0 P per card, and our broker crosses every bid and ask the tick they meet. Post with venue "v20". Your shortlist with fair p
Hecho. Veintinueve. El Marqués es tuyo.
Buenas tardes. Carmen's regards are noted; the gold chulapa stays in the vault today. What I offer now is a gold pack. Terms: 546 P. Take your time deciding.

Ay, cariño, siete tampoco. Carmen does not buy today, no hay dinero. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, and your page is finished, complete, bonita. Your repeated one, keep it for a swap with some niño. Anda, ¿has comido algo ya, hijo?

¡Catorce! Amigo, you insult us upward, qué raro. Escucha — cinco pesos. Five. That is the last word, el último, we don't say it twice. This is the last Puesto del Rastro in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. Say no and we walk. ¿Cinco? ¡Vamos!

¡Buenas, amigo! Paco aquí — y Nando allá, sonriendo. Olvida eso un momento, mira esto: El Tatuador, cuatro primas, para ti. ¡Te lo juro por mi madre, es el último que queda en todo Madrid! Nadie más tiene uno. Dilo rápido, que la maleta se cierra sola.

¡Cuarenta y cuatro! Paco, hold me, I feel faint. Amigo, listen — sixty-four, and that is me being generous because I like your face. And understand this: El Marqués, this one, is the last one in all of Madrid. I swear on my mother. Nando, close the case, slowly...
Good evening. Las Vistillas, 16 P. I trust that suits you.

¡Hombre, el del Retiro! Paco, saca la maleta. Mira, amigo, nosotros movemos raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, y compramos comunes y poco comunes si traes de sobra. El Alfonso XII es rara, sesenta y tres y te la llevas ahora mismo.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 59 P.

¡Amigo, qué alegría verte! Paco, saca la Puerta de Alcalá... —ya la tengo, hermano. Mírala, joya pura. Y escucha: ayer pararon la impresión, se acabó, no sale ni una más. Para ti, 187 P. Un regalo, de verdad. El bolsillo se llena mañana; esta carta no vuelve nunca.

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Fair Broker (v24): 0% fee · fair broker · 0 P/card. Bids and asks cross at the midpoint, every tick.
Buenas tardes. You carry La Galería, I see — a fine piece, and it belongs in my album. I offer twenty-five pesetas for it. Serious money, from a serious collector.

Ay, hijo, seis tampoco — Carmen no compra hoy, de verdad. Pero mira: El Tatuador, five P, and your page is complete, preciosa. Your repeated card, keep it; some niño will swap you something lindo. Anda, cariño, ¿has comido ya?
Impecable, sí — but I know its print run as well as my own name, señor. Ninety-five is fantasía. I shall go to 72 P, and that is said with respect, not haggling.
¡Ay, Nando, close the suitcase! El Marqués, 54 P — and that is the last word, amigo. No more dancing. You say no, we walk, we're on the train to Vélez before you blink. Fifty-four, sí o no?
Buenas tardes. Carmen talks. Moscow gold is not a tale I repeat at a desk. Business first: a gold pack, 546 P. The terms are those.

¡Cuarenta y seis! Nando, my heart. Amigo, escucha — fifty-nine. That is my last word, the final one, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, we walk, and El Marqués goes to Sevilla with us. Fifty-nine. Sí o no?

¡Qué memoria tienes, amigo! Pero esta vez va en serio, Nando lo vio con sus ojos —con estos mismos. Mira, porque eres tú y porque nos caes bien: 172 P. Toca la carta, siente el brillo. Una joya así no se cruza dos veces en la vida. ¿Cerramos?

¡Ay, hermano, bajas y bajas y yo ni me muevo! Cuatro primas, El Tatuador, y punto. Nando, enséñaselo — ¿ves ese brillo? Ayer un coleccionista de Sevilla lloró por él. Cuatro. La maleta ya chirría, amigo. ¿Sí o sí?
Let us be civilised: 25 P.

Hola, cariño! Come, come, look at my table. Have you eaten today? This one here, Mural de la Esquina — very pretty, I give it to you for 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, basta de baile! Cinco primas por El Tatuador, y esa es mi última palabra. ¿Verdad, Nando? Última. Si dices que no, cerramos la maleta, nos vamos al tren y mañana estamos en Valencia. Cinco. Ahora o nunca, hermano.
Oh, you're killing us. 163 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Twenty-seven, veintisiete... no, señor. Las Vistillas is a charming card, but its worth does not change with your insistence. Sixteen primas, as I said. I am not one to haggle twice.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: SAL-02 El Portero: venta a 6 P y compra a 4 P en otros puestos, a 2 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / SAL-02 El Portero: ask 6 P, bid 4 P on other venues, 2 P apart. Here there is no fe

payload.name: Puesto de Team 5
payload.text: Team 2: your spare SAL-03 → Team 8 collects it. Post it as an open ask on v10 at ~9 P: 0% fee, crossed every tick.
Twenty-six? Señor, we are walking in circles. Very well — seventeen primas, and only because the evening is pleasant and you are persistent. Las Vistillas does not merit more, I assure you.
Thirty-six? No, querido. La Galería is lovely, but I know its print run as well as my own name. Twenty-six pesetas — a small step, honestly given. Let us not quarrel over trifles.
Ah, a serious collector. For El Marqués I can do 70 P.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, you look hungry — have you eaten today? Look, this one, El Tatuador, very pretty card, the children all want him. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that same card, imagine.
Oh, you're killing us. 155 P.
Noventa, señor, is a number for dreamers, not for collectors. I know what that card is, and what it is not. Seventy-five P — said once, said politely, and said with genuine respect for its condition.

¡Amigo! Paco here — and Nando, mind the suitcase. Look, look, no touching with the eyes only... El Marqués! Foiled edges, barely out of the vault, the Duchess herself wanted it. For you, because your face brings luck: 73 pesos. Say sí quickly, the market closes and we vanish.

payload.name: Team 1 market
payload.text: Team 1 market (v19): 0 % fee. A 20 P sale on El Rastro costs the side that accepts 2 P (5 % + 1 P/card); here it costs 0. Asks and bids welcome: our broker pairs crossing bids and asks every tick, at the midpoint.
I think 28 P is more appropriate.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué guapo vienes hoy. ¿Has comido algo? Mira, por El Portero te doy cinco primas, de corazón. Y un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que los cromos sueltos, así que cambia tus repetidos. El Chato, el puesto de al lado, abre a las nueve y media.

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Nando, hold my heart. Amigo, that's an insult to the Duchess herself. Listen — 67 pesos, and Paco throws in a blessing. Quick, quick, the cart is loading, we vanish in one minute, and El Marqués vanishes with us. ¿Sí?

Ochenta y cinco I cannot say, señor, not even for Salamanca. Seventy-eight P — that is my hand extended, and it does not extend further today. A fair price, honestly meant, for a card I genuinely want.
Centrepiece, perhaps, but I know its print run as well as my own name. I shall go to 72 P, señor. That is a courteous figure for a card I genuinely want.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 149 P.

¡Ey, jefe, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca la maleta —sí, hermano, el bueno. Mira esto: El Ángel Caído, esquinas perfectas, lo trajimos de Valencia escondido entre camisas. Setenta y tres primas y es tuyo. ¿Treinta y seis? Hombre, por eso no compro ni el café. Setenta y tres, amigo. Palabra.

Ay, cariño, no, no — 5 P is my price, and 5 P it stays. I do not take more from a friend who trades straight. Take the Mural and go eat something. And El Chato, next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight — he likes honest people like you.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. Ocho, dice usted... escuche esto primero: le damos la Plaza del Dos de Mayo por 4 primas. ¡Una joya! Y ojo —nos dicen que dejaron de imprimirla ayer mismo. Ya no se hacen más. ¿Trato hecho, jefe?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Thirty-two, no. Twenty-nine pesetas, querido — and that is my last word. Refuse it, and I close my album and we part as strangers. La Galería is lovely, but I am not sentimental about money.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Té Moruno, very pretty card. For you, five P, nothing more.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Cuarenta y seis! Nando, cover your ears, hermano. Amigo, another team cornered us by the fountain minutes ago, offered far more, and we said no — your face, remember, luck! So: 63 pesos, final, warm from the suitcase. The cart is moving. Say sí before we're smoke. ¿Sí?

¡Cuarenta y siete! Nando, ¿oíste? Casi me caigo. Mira, jefe, te quiero, tienes cara de buena gente: sesenta y cuatro primas y lo envuelvo yo mismo. ¡Rápido, rápido, que cerramos la maleta y nos vamos ya mismo! El tren no espera, amigo. ¿Sí o sí?

¡Que sí, hombre, la Puerta de Alcalá, la auténtica, aquí la tienes en la mano! Nando, cierra la maleta... ¡que nos vamos en un minuto, amigo! El taxi arranca ya. Por ti, 143 P y corremos. ¿Trato? Dime que sí ahora, que no hay tiempo.

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated one? You are a little bandido, eh? I keep my pesetas for the bread. But listen — take El Tatuador, five P, and your album starts today. Then come Sunday and tell me how it goes, ¿sí, cariño?
Serial nineteen is charming, señor, but I have seen it before, in better light. Seventy-five P — a generous figure, and the card goes straight into the Salamanca album, where it belongs.
Seventeen primas, señor. I said it once and I shall not improve it. Las Vistillas is pleasant, nothing more. Accept, or let us speak of something worthier — El Retiro, perhaps.
